content.text:
Personalized Weight-Loss Plan
Client: Male, 25 y, 175 cm, 80 kg — Goal: weight loss — Activity: moderately active — No medical limitations

Quick numbers (estimates)
- BMR (Mifflin–St Jeor): ~1,774 kcal/day
- Estimated TDEE (moderately active, x1.55): ~2,750 kcal/day
- Recommended calorie target for steady weight loss: ~2,200 kcal/day (≈500 kcal deficit → ~0.5 kg/week). Range: 1,900–2,400 kcal depending on weekly progress.
- Protein target: 1.6–2.2 g/kg → 130–176 g/day (aim 140–160 g).
- Fat: 20–30% of calories → ~50–80 g/day.
- Carbs: remainder → ~200–300 g/day.

1) Workout plan (practical, progressive)
Principles: 3–4 strength sessions/week (compound-focused), 2 cardio sessions, 1 active recovery/rest. Warm up 5–10 min before work sets; cool down and stretch after. Aim for progressive overload (add weight or reps every 1–2 weeks).

Option A — 6-day structure (recommended for faster results)
- Day 1 — Upper Strength (Push + Pull)
  - Warm-up: 5–8 min row or bike + shoulder mobility
  - Barbell bench press: 4 × 6–8
  - Bent-over barbell or dumbbell row: 4 × 6–8
  - Overhead press (standing dumbbell/barbell): 3 × 8–10
  - Pull-ups or lat pulldown: 3 × 6–10
  - Incline dumbbell fly or cable: 2 × 10–12
  - Plank: 3 × 45–60 sec
- Day 2 — Lower Strength
  - Warm-up: 5–8 min bike + hip mobility
  - Back squat or goblet squat: 4 × 6–8
  - Romanian deadlift: 3 × 8–10
  - Bulgarian split squat or lunges: 3 × 8–10 each leg
  - Calf raises: 3 × 12–15
  - Hanging leg raise or deadbug: 3 × 10–15
- Day 3 — Cardio / Active Recovery
  - Option A: 30–40 min moderate-intensity (jog, cycle, rowing)
  - Option B (time-crunched): 20 min HIIT (e.g., 8–10 × 20s sprint/40s easy)
  - Mobility 10–15 min
- Day 4 — Upper Hypertrophy / Accessories
  - Incline dumbbell press: 3 × 8–10
  - Single-arm dumbbell row: 3 × 8–10
  - Lateral raises: 3 × 12–15
  - Face pulls: 3 × 12–15
  - Biceps curls & triceps pushdowns: 2 × 10–12 each
  - Side plank: 2 × 30–45 sec each
- Day 5 — Lower Power/Posterior Focus
  - Deadlift (conventional or trap bar): 4 × 4–6 OR lighter 3 × 6–8 if new to deadlift
  - Front squat or goblet squat: 3 × 6–8
  - Glute bridge / hip thrust: 3 × 8–12
  - Hamstring curl: 3 × 10–12
  - Farmer carry or 2–3 min walk for conditioning
- Day 6 — Long steady-state cardio or HIIT + mobility
  - 40–60 min brisk walk, bike, or easy run OR 25–30 min HIIT
- Day 7 — Rest or gentle mobility/yoga

Option B — 3-day full-body (if busy)
- Full-body sessions on Mon/Wed/Fri: 3 compound lifts (squat/press/pull), 3 sets each, 6–10 reps, plus core. Add 2 cardio sessions midweek + weekend walk.

Progression rules
- If you complete top rep range for all sets in two consecutive workouts, increase weight by 2.5–5% (or add 1–2 reps per set).
- Track weights and reps in a training log.
- Prioritize form; reduce load to correct technique.

Daily baseline activity
- Target 8,000–12,000 steps/day for extra calorie burn and health benefits.

2) Meal plan (flexible, simple, ~2,200 kcal example)
Guidelines
- Protein at each meal (helps satiety and preserves muscle).
- Fill half the plate with vegetables + moderate whole grains + lean protein + healthy fats.
- Hydrate: 2–3 L water/day (more around workouts).
- Prepare/portion meals ahead to avoid last-minute choices.

Sample single-day plan (~2,200 kcal; macros ~150 g protein / 70 g fat / 210 g carbs)
- Breakfast (≈480 kcal)
  - 60 g rolled oats cooked with water/milk
  - 1 scoop whey protein (≈25 g protein) mixed in
  - 1 medium banana
  - 1 tbsp almond butter
  - (Macros ≈ 35g P / 55g C / 15g F)
- Morning snack (≈200 kcal)
  - 200 g nonfat Greek yogurt + 50 g mixed berries
  - (≈20g P / 20g C / 0–3g F)
- Lunch (≈650 kcal)
  - 150–170 g grilled chicken breast
  - 75–100 g dry weight quinoa or brown rice (cooked portion ~1–1.5 cups)
  - Large salad / steamed veg with 1 tbsp olive oil or dressing
  - (≈45–50g P / 60–70g C / 20–25g F)
- Afternoon snack (≈200 kcal)
  - Apple + 20–25 g almonds or 1 serving hummus + carrot sticks
  - (≈5–8g P / 25g C / 10–12g F)
- Dinner (≈670 kcal)
  - 150 g salmon or lean steak (or tofu for variety)
  - 200 g sweet potato (baked)
  - Steamed broccoli / mixed vegetables
  - 1 tsp olive oil or small salad dressing
  - (≈45–50g P / 50–60g C / 20–25g F)

Swap options (same-calorie equivalents)
- Protein: chicken, turkey, lean beef, fish, tempeh, tofu, eggs, cottage cheese, Greek yogurt.
- Carbs: oats, brown rice, quinoa, whole-wheat pasta, potatoes, whole-grain bread.
- Fats: olive oil, avocado, nuts, seeds, nut butter.

7-day rotating plan idea (repeatable)
- Day A: Oat + whey; chicken + rice + veg; salmon + sweet potato + veg
- Day B: Eggs + whole-grain toast + avocado; turkey chili + salad; stir-fry tofu + brown rice
- Day C: Smoothie (fruit + spinach + protein + oats); tuna salad wrap; lean steak + baked potato
- Keep snacks: Greek yogurt, cottage cheese, fruit, nuts, hummus+veggies, protein shakes.

Meal prep tips
- Cook 2–3 proteins in bulk (chicken, turkey, tofu).
- Pre-cook grains and portion into containers.
- Chop vegetables for quick salads & stir-fries.
- Portion snacks (nuts, yogurt) ahead.

3) Daily / weekly structure (example weekly calendar)
- Monday: Upper Strength + 8–10k steps
  - Meals timed: Breakfast 7:30, Snack 10:30, Lunch 13:00, Snack 16:00, Dinner 19:00
- Tuesday: Lower Strength + walk after dinner
- Wednesday: Cardio (30–40 min steady) + mobility
- Thursday: Upper Hypertrophy + evening walk
- Friday: Lower (deadlift focus) + mobility
- Saturday: Long steady-state cardio or HIIT (choose one) + active recreation
- Sunday: Rest + stretching/yoga + meal prep for the week

Typical day (if working a 9–5)
- 06:30 — Wake, 300–400 ml water
- 07:00 — Light mobility + 10 min warm-up (if training morning) or gym
- 07:30 — Breakfast
- 09:30–11:00 — Morning snack as needed
- 13:00 — Lunch
- 16:00 — Pre-work snack if training after work
- 18:00–19:30 — Workout (strength or cardio)
- 20:00 — Dinner
- 22:30 — Bedtime target (aim 7–9 hrs sleep)

4) Useful recommendations & tracking
- Track: body weight once weekly (same day/time, e.g., Monday morning fasted), plus monthly progress photos and circumference measurements (waist/hips/chest).
- Expectation: safe weight loss ~0.4–1 kg/week. Adjust calories if rate is faster or slower than desired.
- If no weight loss after 2–4 weeks: reduce daily intake by 150–300 kcal or add 1–2 weekly cardio sessions.
- If losing too fast (>1.5% bodyweight/week) increase calories slightly to protect muscle.
- Sleep: target 7–9 hours/night for recovery and appetite regulation.
- Hydration: 2–3 L/day; more on hot days or heavy sweating.
- Alcohol: limit — alcohol adds calories and can impair recovery.
- Supplements (optional, evidence-backed):
  - Creatine monohydrate 5 g/day (improves performance, preserves muscle)
  - Whey protein to meet protein goals if needed
  - Fish oil (omega-3) 1–2 g EPA+DHA/day
  - Vitamin D if low exposure (test or 1,000–2,000 IU/day typical)
- Injury prevention: learn proper form (consider 2–4 sessions with a qualified coach), prioritize mobility and soft tissue work.
- Consistency > perfection: plan for 80% adherence; occasional treats are OK.
- Adjustability: every 4 weeks reassess weight, performance (are lifts getting stronger?), and energy. If strength is dropping and fatigue high, add a refeed or increase calories and rest.

Sample grocery list
- Proteins: chicken breast, turkey mince, salmon, canned tuna, eggs, Greek yogurt, cottage cheese
- Carbs: oats, brown rice, quinoa, sweet potatoes, whole-grain bread
- Veg & fruit: mixed greens, broccoli, spinach, bell peppers, tomatoes, bananas, berries, apples
- Fats: olive oil, avocado, mixed nuts, almond butter
- Extras: spices, low-sodium soy sauce, hummus, protein powder, coffee/tea

Safety & final notes
- You have no reported medical conditions, but stop and consult a physician if you experience chest pain, dizziness, or other concerning symptoms.
- If new to lifting, start with lighter weights and focus on form; consider 2–4 sessions with a coach to learn key lifts safely.
- Reassess and adjust: after 4 weeks review weight and strength. If losing too slowly, reduce calories modestly or add cardio; if losing too fast or performance drops, increase calories.

If you want, I can:
- Create a printable 4-week workout calendar with exact sets/reps and progression.
- Build a 7-day meal plan with grocery lists and recipes tailored to 2,000 / 2,200 / 2,500 kcal targets.
- Convert this into a PDF layout-ready structure.

Which add-on would you like?
